incidents.story: When Ravana heard of Kumbhakarna's death, he fell senseless with sorrow. He wept that he had lost his right arm and that life without his brother meant nothing. For the first time, he remembered Vibhishana's warnings with regret.

incidents.title: Ravana's Sons Fall
incidents.story: To comfort their father, Ravana's sons Trishiras, Narantaka, and Devantaka went into battle with their uncles. Angada struck down Narantaka, and Hanuman defeated Devantaka and Trishiras. Nila and Rishabha struck down the uncles Mahodara and Mahaparshva, and one by one Ravana's proud warriors fell.

incidents.title: Lakshmana Defeats Atikaya
incidents.story: Atikaya, a giant son of Ravana, wore armour given by Brahma that no ordinary arrow could pierce. Lakshmana fought him long and hard. Then the Wind God whispered advice, and Lakshmana used the Brahmastra to bring Atikaya down.

incidents.title: Indrajit's Brahmastra
incidents.story: Furious at his brothers' deaths, Indrajit made himself invisible and released the Brahmastra. Its arrows struck down Rama, Lakshmana, and countless monkeys. Out of respect for Lord Brahma, the brothers did not resist the weapon, and the battlefield fell silent.

incidents.title: Jambavan Sends Hanuman
incidents.story: In the night, Vibhishana and Hanuman searched the battlefield with torches. They found the aged Jambavan, wounded and almost blind, who asked first whether Hanuman lived. If Hanuman lives, he said, we all live. He sent Hanuman to the Himalayas for healing herbs.

incidents.title: Hanuman Brings the Herb Mountain
incidents.story: Hanuman flew to the Himalayas, but the magical herbs hid themselves from him. Unwilling to waste time, he lifted the whole mountain peak and carried it back to Lanka. The very fragrance of the herbs healed Rama, Lakshmana, and the entire army.

incidents.title: Kumbha and Nikumbha Fall
incidents.story: Kumbhakarna's sons Kumbha and Nikumbha came to avenge their father. Kumbha fought Sugriva fiercely, but the monkey king struck him down with his fist. Then Hanuman wrestled the mighty Nikumbha, who swung a great iron club, and defeated him.

incidents.title: Rama Defeats Makaraksha
incidents.story: Makaraksha, son of the demon Khara whom Rama had slain in the forest, came seeking revenge. He challenged Rama boldly. After a fierce duel, Rama struck him down with the fire weapon of Agni, and the rakshasas fled back into Lanka.

incidents.title: The Illusory Sita Slain
incidents.story: Indrajit created a false Sita by magic and struck her down before Hanuman's eyes. Hanuman rushed back with the terrible news, and Rama fainted with grief. It was a cruel trick meant to break their spirit while Indrajit went to perform a secret ritual.

incidents.title: Vibhishana Reveals the Secret
incidents.story: Vibhishana assured Rama that Ravana would never let Sita be killed, and the death was only an illusion. He revealed that Indrajit was performing a sacrifice at Nikumbhila that would make him unbeatable. Lakshmana hurried there with Vibhishana and Hanuman to stop it.

incidents.title: Lakshmana Duels Indrajit
incidents.story: Lakshmana interrupted the sacrifice and challenged Indrajit to fight. Their duel was long and terrible, and both were covered with wounds. Arrows filled the sky like rain, and even the gods watched from above, holding their breath.

incidents.title: Indrajit Falls
incidents.story: At last Lakshmana fitted the arrow of Indra to his bow and spoke a vow: if Rama is truly righteous and truthful, let this arrow slay Indrajit. The arrow flew and struck off Indrajit's head. Rama embraced his brave brother, and Sushena healed his wounds.

incidents.title: Ravana's Rage
incidents.story: Hearing of Indrajit's death, Ravana went mad with grief and anger. He seized a sword and rushed to kill Sita. His wise minister Suparshva stopped him, reminding him that it was shameful to harm a woman, and urged him to face Rama in battle instead.

incidents.title: Ravana's Last Generals Fall
incidents.story: Ravana sent his last commanders to battle. Sugriva struck down Virupaksha and then the mighty Mahodara in fierce duels. Angada slew Mahaparshva with a single blow. Now Ravana had no generals left, and he rode out himself.

incidents.title: The Shakti Strikes Lakshmana
incidents.story: Ravana hurled a fearsome spear called a Shakti at Vibhishana. To protect his friend, Lakshmana stepped in front, and the spear struck him in the chest. Lakshmana fell, and Rama pulled the spear out with his own hands, weeping for his brother.

incidents.title: Sushena Heals Lakshmana
incidents.story: The monkey physician Sushena sent Hanuman to bring a mountain of healing herbs once more. Sushena crushed the herbs and let Lakshmana breathe their scent. Lakshmana rose, healed and strong, and urged Rama to slay Ravana before the sun set.

incidents.title: Matali Brings Indra's Chariot
incidents.story: Seeing Rama fighting on foot while Ravana rode a chariot, Indra sent his own divine chariot with his charioteer Matali. It shone like the sun and carried heavenly weapons. Rama bowed to it respectfully and climbed aboard for the final battle.

incidents.title: Agastya Teaches Aditya Hridayam
incidents.story: As Rama paused, tired from battle, the great sage Agastya came to him. He taught Rama the Aditya Hridayam, a sacred hymn to the Sun God that gives strength and victory. Rama recited it three times and felt new energy fill his heart.

incidents.title: The Heads That Grew Back
incidents.story: Rama and Ravana fought a duel unlike any other. Each time Rama cut off one of Ravana's heads, a new one grew back in its place. This happened again and again, and Rama wondered how this mighty enemy could be defeated.

incidents.title: The Brahmastra Is Released
incidents.story: Matali reminded Rama of the Brahmastra, the weapon given to him by the sage Agastya. Rama chanted sacred words and released it. The arrow blazed like fire, filling the sky with light as it flew straight toward Ravana's heart.

incidents.title: Ravana Falls
incidents.story: The Brahmastra pierced Ravana's chest, and he fell from his chariot, never to rise again. Flowers rained from the heavens, and the gods sang Rama's praise. Good had triumphed over evil, and the world was free from fear.

incidents.title: Vibhishana Mourns His Brother
incidents.story: Vibhishana wept beside his fallen brother, remembering his strength and greatness. Rama comforted him, saying that enmity ends with death. He told Vibhishana that Ravana was now as dear to him as to Vibhishana, and asked him to perform the last rites with honour.

incidents.title: Mandodari's Lament
incidents.story: Ravana's queen Mandodari came to the battlefield and wept over her husband. She remembered how mighty he had been, and said that his desire for Sita had brought about his end. Then Vibhishana performed Ravana's funeral with the full honours of a king, as Rama had wished.

incidents.title: Vibhishana Crowned King of Lanka
incidents.story: Lakshmana anointed Vibhishana as king of Lanka with water from the sea, just as Rama had promised. The rakshasas welcomed their new ruler with joy. Under Vibhishana, Lanka would be guided by dharma and kindness.

incidents.title: Hanuman Brings Sita the News
incidents.story: Rama sent Hanuman to tell Sita of the victory. Sita was so overjoyed that at first she could not speak. When Hanuman offered to punish the rakshasis who had troubled her, Sita forgave them, saying that a noble person shows mercy even to those who do wrong.

incidents.title: Sita's Trial by Fire
incidents.story: Sita was brought before Rama in front of the whole army. Rama spoke stern words about her long stay in Ravana's city. Deeply hurt but firm in her purity, Sita asked Lakshmana to build a fire and, praying to Agni, stepped into the flames.

incidents.title: Agni Restores Sita
incidents.story: The fire god Agni rose from the flames holding Sita in his arms, unburnt and shining. He declared that she was pure in thought, word, and deed. Rama joyfully took her back, explaining that he had always known her purity and wanted the world to see it.

incidents.title: Dasharatha Appears from Heaven
incidents.story: Rama's father, King Dasharatha, appeared in a heavenly chariot, glowing with light. He embraced Rama and blessed him, Lakshmana, and Sita. At Rama's request, he forgave Kaikeyi and Bharata, and then returned to the heavenly realm.

incidents.title: Indra Revives the Monkeys
incidents.story: Indra, king of the gods, offered Rama a boon. Rama asked only that all the monkeys and bears who had died for his cause be brought back to life. Indra granted it, and the fallen warriors rose as if waking from sleep.

incidents.title: The Flight on Pushpaka
incidents.story: Vibhishana gave Rama the flying Pushpaka chariot, and Rama took his friends with him to Ayodhya. As they flew, Rama showed Sita the battlefield, the great bridge, Kishkindha, and the forests where he had searched for her. Each place held a memory of their journey.

incidents.title: Rama Visits Bharadvaja
incidents.story: On the fifth day after the fourteen years ended, Rama reached the ashram of the sage Bharadvaja. The sage welcomed him lovingly, gave news of Bharata and Ayodhya, and blessed him. Rama stayed the night and prepared to go home.

incidents.title: Hanuman Sent Ahead to Bharata
incidents.story: Rama sent Hanuman ahead to tell Bharata that he was coming home. Hanuman found Bharata at Nandigrama, living simply as a hermit with Rama's sandals on the throne. Bharata was so overjoyed by the news that he embraced Hanuman with tears.

incidents.title: Bharata Welcomes Rama Home
incidents.story: Bharata came to meet Rama with the whole city of Ayodhya. When the brothers met, they embraced with tears of joy. Bharata placed Rama's sandals back on his feet, saying he was returning the kingdom he had kept safe for fourteen years.

incidents.title: The Coronation of Rama
incidents.story: At last Rama was crowned king of Ayodhya by the sage Vasishtha. Sacred waters from rivers and seas were poured over him, and Sita sat by his side. The people cheered with joy, and the gods sent blessings from above.

incidents.title: Hanuman's Pearl Necklace
incidents.story: After the coronation, Rama gave Sita a beautiful pearl necklace. Sita looked at Rama, and with his gentle nod, she gave it to Hanuman, the one most loyal and brave. Hanuman accepted it with devotion, honoured above all.

incidents.title: Rama Rajya
incidents.story: Rama ruled Ayodhya with justice and love for many years. In his kingdom no one suffered from hunger, sickness, or fear, and people lived in peace. Rama Rajya became the ideal of a perfect kingdom, remembered for all time.

incidents.title: Agastya Tells of the Rakshasas
incidents.story: After Rama became king, the great sage Agastya came to Ayodhya and told him the old history of the rakshasas. Long ago, the three brothers Malyavan, Sumali and Mali grew mighty and troubled the gods. Vishnu defeated them, and the survivors fled from Lanka to the underworld.

incidents.title: The Birth of Ravana
incidents.story: Sumali wished his family to rise again, so his daughter Kaikasi married the sage Vishrava. She bore Ravana with ten heads, the giant Kumbhakarna, a daughter named Shurpanakha, and the gentle Vibhishana. From one home came very different hearts, and their choices would shape the whole Ramayana.

incidents.title: The Brothers Win Their Boons
incidents.story: The three brothers performed fierce tapas for thousands of years. Ravana offered his heads one by one, and Brahma granted that no god, demon or spirit could kill him, though in his pride he did not ask for safety from humans. Kumbhakarna was given long sleep, and Vibhishana asked always to love dharma.

incidents.title: Ravana Seizes Lanka and Pushpaka
incidents.story: Lanka was then ruled by Kubera, Ravana's half-brother and the lord of wealth. Proud of his boon, Ravana demanded the golden city, and Kubera left it peacefully on their father's advice. Later Ravana attacked Kubera, defeated him in battle, and took his flying chariot, the Pushpaka.

incidents.title: Ravana Lifts Mount Kailasa
incidents.story: Flying over Kailasa, Ravana's chariot suddenly stopped, and Nandi warned him that Shiva dwelt there. In anger, Ravana pushed his arms under the mountain and lifted it. Shiva gently pressed down with his toe, trapping Ravana's arms. His loud cry earned him the name Ravana, and after long praise Shiva released him.

incidents.title: The Curse of Vedavati
incidents.story: In the Himalayan forest, Ravana met Vedavati, a pure maiden doing tapas to win Vishnu as her husband. When he seized her by the hair, she cut it off and entered a fire. Before leaving her body, she vowed to be born again to bring about his ruin, and it is said she was reborn as Sita.

incidents.title: Indrajit Captures Indra
incidents.story: Ravana marched on heaven and fought the gods. When the battle turned against his father, Ravana's son Meghanada used his magic to vanish, bound Indra, and carried him to Lanka. Brahma came to free Indra and gave the young warrior the name Indrajit, conqueror of Indra.

incidents.title: Kartavirya Arjuna Defeats Ravana
incidents.story: By the Narmada river, Ravana sat worshipping Shiva with flowers. Upstream, the thousand-armed king Kartavirya Arjuna held back the water while playing, and the flood swept Ravana's offerings away. Ravana attacked in rage, but the king overpowered him and kept him captive until the sage Pulastya asked for his release.

incidents.title: Vali Carries Ravana Across the Seas
incidents.story: Ravana wished to fight Vali, the mighty vanara king, and crept up behind him while he prayed by the southern ocean. Vali simply tucked Ravana under his arm and flew to all four oceans to finish his prayers. Humbled, Ravana asked for friendship, and they became allies.

incidents.title: Baby Hanuman Leaps at the Sun
incidents.story: As a hungry baby, Hanuman saw the rising sun and thought it was a ripe fruit. He leapt into the sky to catch it. Indra struck him with his thunderbolt, hurting his jaw, and his angry father Vayu stopped the air from moving. The gods then healed Hanuman and blessed him with many great powers.

incidents.title: Hanuman Forgets His Strength
incidents.story: Young Hanuman was so full of energy that he played pranks on the sages in their hermitages. The sages lovingly cursed him to forget his powers until someone reminded him. That is why, much later, Jambavan had to remind him of his strength before his great leap to Lanka.

incidents.title: The Friends Return Home
incidents.story: When the coronation festivities ended, Rama gave rich gifts to Sugriva, Vibhishana, Angada, Jambavan and all the vanaras and rakshasas who had helped him. With tears of love, they took leave of him. Each returned to his own kingdom, carrying the memory of Rama's kindness.

incidents.title: Hanuman's Wish
incidents.story: As he took leave, Hanuman asked Rama for one gift. He wished that his love for Rama would never fade, and that he might live on earth for as long as Rama's story is told. Rama gladly granted it and embraced him, saying he could never repay Hanuman's service.

incidents.title: Sita's Wish to Visit the Hermitages
incidents.story: Rama and Sita spent happy days in the palace gardens of Ayodhya. When Sita was expecting a child, Rama asked what she wished for. She longed to visit the peaceful hermitages of the sages on the banks of the Ganga, and Rama promised that she would go.

incidents.title: The Talk in the City
incidents.story: Rama asked his friend Bhadra what the people of Ayodhya were saying about him. Bhadra replied that they praised his victory, but some doubted Sita because she had lived in Ravana's palace. Later tellings say Rama overheard a washerman, but in Valmiki the news comes through Bhadra, and it deeply troubles the king.

incidents.title: Rama's Painful Decision
incidents.story: Rama called his brothers and, with a heavy heart, told them of the people's talk. Though he knew Sita was pure, he felt a king must keep the trust of his people. He asked Lakshmana to take Sita to the hermitages she wished to see and leave her near Valmiki's ashram.

incidents.title: Lakshmana Leaves Sita by the Ganga
incidents.story: Lakshmana drove Sita to the Ganga and took her across the river. There, weeping, he told her Rama's command. Sita was heartbroken, yet she sent Rama a gentle message to rule his people well, and said she carried his child. Lakshmana bowed to her and sadly returned.

incidents.title: Valmiki Shelters Sita
incidents.story: The young sons of the sages saw Sita weeping alone and ran to tell Valmiki. The kind sage came at once, comforted her, and said he knew she was innocent. He led her to the women of the hermitage, who welcomed and cared for her like a daughter.

incidents.title: The Birth of Lava and Kusha
incidents.story: On the night Shatrughna stayed at Valmiki's hermitage, Sita gave birth to twin sons. Valmiki protected the babies with blessings using sacred kusha grass. The elder, touched with the tips of the grass, was named Kusha, and the younger, touched with its lower part, was named Lava.

incidents.title: Shatrughna Slays Lavanasura
incidents.story: The sages of the Yamuna forest asked Rama for help against Lavana, a cruel rakshasa who held Shiva's mighty trident. Rama sent Shatrughna with a divine arrow. Shatrughna waited at the gate so Lavana could not reach his trident, then slew him. He founded the city of Madhura, later called Mathura, and ruled it well.

incidents.title: The Ashvamedha with a Golden Sita
incidents.story: Rama performed the great horse sacrifice in the Naimisha forest by the Gomati river. Kings and sages came from everywhere. Rama never took another wife, so a golden image of Sita sat beside him in her place, showing his lifelong faithfulness to her.

incidents.title: Lava and Kusha Capture the Horse
incidents.story: In later tellings, such as the Padma Purana and Jaimini's Ashvamedha, Lava and Kusha caught the sacrificial horse in the forest and refused to let it go. They bravely fought the warriors sent to win it back. This story is not found in Valmiki's Ramayana, but it is loved across India.

incidents.title: Lava and Kusha Sing the Ramayana
incidents.story: Valmiki sent Lava and Kusha to sing his poem at Rama's sacrifice. Dressed as young ascetics, they sang the Ramayana so sweetly that the whole assembly listened in wonder. Rama offered them gold, but they gently refused, saying they lived in the forest and needed nothing.

incidents.title: Rama Recognises His Sons
incidents.story: As the twins sang day after day, Rama learned that they were the sons of Sita. His heart was filled with love and longing. He sent messengers to Valmiki, asking Sita to come before the assembly and declare her purity so that the people would accept her.

incidents.title: Sita Returns to the Earth
incidents.story: Valmiki led Sita into the assembly and declared that she was pure. Sita said that if she had never thought of anyone but Rama, Mother Earth should receive her. The ground opened, the Earth goddess rose on a divine throne, took Sita in her arms, and vanished as flowers fell from the sky.

incidents.title: The Passing of the Queens
incidents.story: Rama ruled for many years in grief and duty. In time, his mothers Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi grew old and left this world. Having lived lives of devotion, they joined King Dasharatha in heaven, and Rama honoured them with sacred rites and gifts.

incidents.title: Kingdoms for the Princes
incidents.story: Bharata conquered the land of the Gandharvas and founded the cities of Takshashila and Pushkalavati for his sons Taksha and Pushkala. Lakshmana's sons Angada and Chandraketu were given kingdoms in the land of Karupatha. In this way, Rama's family spread his just rule far and wide.

incidents.title: Time Visits Rama
incidents.story: One day Kala, the spirit of Time, came to Rama dressed as an ascetic with a message from Brahma. He asked to speak alone, and Rama ordered that anyone who disturbed them must be given up. Lakshmana stood guard. Kala gently reminded Rama that his work on earth was complete.

incidents.title: Lakshmana's Great Sacrifice
incidents.story: The fiery sage Durvasa came and demanded to see Rama at once, threatening to curse the whole kingdom. To save everyone, Lakshmana entered the room, knowing the price. To keep his word, Rama gave up his beloved brother. Lakshmana went calmly to the Sarayu and left his body, and the gods welcomed him to heaven.

incidents.title: Rama's Last Journey
incidents.story: Rama crowned Kusha and Lava as kings and walked to the Sarayu, followed by Bharata, Shatrughna, and the people of Ayodhya. Entering the sacred river, Rama returned to his divine form as Vishnu. All who had followed him with love were given a place in heaven, while Hanuman stayed on earth.
